items.stem: A connector returns a customer record that a workflow will use to send an email. What is the safe design?

options.text: A human confirms the record is correct before the consequential action runs
options.rationale: Correct: consequential actions should have a human-in-the-loop check.

options.text: Send the email automatically with no check
options.rationale: Acting on unverified tool output is risky.

options.text: Assume the connector is always right
options.rationale: Tool outputs can be wrong or stale and must be verified.
Logging aids auditability and should be kept.

items.explanation: Correct: consequential actions should have a human-in-the-loop check.

items.stem: Which TWO reflect least-privilege connector permissions? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Granting only the access a task actually requires
Reviewing and revoking access that is no longer needed
options.rationale: Correct: stale permissions should be removed.

options.text: Granting broad access because it is convenient
options.rationale: Convenience is not a security rationale.

options.text: What data the connector can access and expose

options.rationale: Popularity is not an access assessment.

options.text: Nothing; connect first and check later
options.rationale: Connecting first can expose data unintentionally.
